title: Apply for a pyrotechnician's licence
summary: This page provides information on how to apply for a pyrotechnician's licence, which allows you to handle fireworks.
intro:
A pyrotechnician's licence allows you to purchase, possess, use, store and transport fireworks.

The licence is valid for 5 years and covers the following types of fireworks:

If you want to use non-aerial fireworks for a single event, you can apply for a fireworks (single use) licence.
who_can_apply: Hold a current NSW security clearance (SC) or provide evidence of lodging one.
Have the relevant qualifications, experience, and knowledge.
Only use the fireworks for an organised public event and have a supporting letter from the local council stating they have no objections.
what_you_need: A current NSW security clearance (SC) or evidence of a security clearance application.
A JP certified copy of any explosives licence issued in any other Australian state, OR a statutory declaration completed by the licence holder who has supervised you during fireworks displays.
A JP certified copy of the front and back of your model rocket membership (if applicable).
Certified copies of qualifications issued by a registered training organisation (if applicable).
If storage is requested, additional documentation is required.

how_to_steps.text: Collect all the required documentation including the material needed for your SC application (if applicable).
Ensure the statutory declaration is completed.
Ensure the JP certified copy of the front and back of your model rocket membership is provided (if applicable)
Submit your application and payment online.

more_info.text: If you're lodging your application for an SC licence at the same time, it will have to be approved before your pyrotechnician's licence application will be processed.

faqs.q: How long is a pyrotechnician's licence valid for?
faqs.a: The licence is valid for 5 years.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a pyrotechnician's licence and a single-use licence?
faqs.a: A pyrotechnician's licence covers general use, while a fireworks (single use) licence is for using non-aerial fireworks for a single event.

faqs.q: What are the basic requirements to apply for the licence?
faqs.a: You must be aged 18 or over, hold a current NSW security clearance (SC) or provide evidence of lodging one, and have the relevant qualifications, experience, and knowledge.
